1.pattern: Pod not Running → read Events → fix the owner (Deployment)

clues.means: Look at STATUS, then read Events with describe
Fix it in place: k set image / k edit deploy
Done only when the NEW pod shows 1/1 Running

traps: Using the deployment name (api) as the container name in set image — the container is nginx
Forgetting -n app → 'No resources found'
Fixing the pod instead of the deployment — the deployment recreates the broken pod
memorise: k describe pod <pod> -n app   # Events: ImagePullBackOff, bad tag
k set image deploy/api nginx=nginx:1.27 -n app

2.pattern: Pod CrashLoopBackOff → logs --previous → fix command in Deployment

clues.means: CrashLoopBackOff: the container starts then exits; read logs --previous
Fix the pod template with k edit deploy
The command in the spec is wrong; set it to sleep 3600

traps: Reading k logs without --previous (the new container may have no output yet)
Editing the pod instead of the deployment
Breaking YAML indentation in the command list

verify.see: 1/1 Running, RESTARTS stays 0 for the new pod

verify.cmd: k get deploy api -n app -o yaml | grep -A3 command

memorise: k edit deploy api -n app   # exit 1 → sleep 3600

3.pattern: Pod Pending → describe Events → lower resource requests

clues.means: The scheduler cannot place it: read Events (Insufficient cpu)
Set the CPU request to exactly 100m on the deployment

traps: Setting --limits instead of --requests
Editing the pod instead of deployment api
Not waiting for the old Pending pod to be replaced

verify.cmd: k get deploy api -n app -o jsonpath='{..resources}'

memorise: k describe pod <pod> -n app   # Insufficient cpu
k set resources deploy api -n app --requests=cpu=100m

4.pattern: Node NotReady → ssh → kubelet stopped → enable --now

clues.means: Kubelet on that node is not reporting: ssh in and check systemctl

clues.q: The fix must survive a reboot
clues.means: Use systemctl enable (not only start)
Start the service by hand: enable --now

traps: systemctl start only — not enabled, lost after reboot
Running systemctl on the control plane instead of node01
Forgetting to exit back before k get nodes
memorise: k describe node node01   # Kubelet stopped posting status

5.pattern: Node NotReady → kubelet fails → fix service file path

clues.means: ssh to node01, check kubelet status and journal
After editing the unit: daemon-reload + restart kubelet

traps: Forgetting systemctl daemon-reload after editing the unit file
Editing the wrong file — use systemctl cat kubelet to find which file has ExecStart
Only starting kubelet without fixing the bad /usr/local/bin path

6.pattern: Service unreachable → no endpoints → fix selector to match labels

clues.means: Check k get endpoints first: empty = selector mismatch
Pods are fine; the Service is the problem

clues.q: Do not delete or recreate the service
clues.means: Change it in place: k set selector or k edit svc

traps: Relabelling the pods instead of fixing the service selector
Copying the pod-template-hash label into the selector
Testing with curl — busybox client has wget

verify.cmd: k exec client -n web -- wget -qO- -T 3 backend-svc

memorise: k describe svc backend-svc -n web   # Selector
k set selector svc backend-svc app=backend -n web
k exec client -n web -- wget -qO- -T 3 backend-svc

7.pattern: Service has endpoints but no answer → fix targetPort

clues.means: targetPort must be 80
k edit svc and change targetPort only

traps: Changing port instead of targetPort
Deleting and re-exposing the service (forbidden)
Thinking endpoints present means everything is fine — check the port after the IP

verify.cmd: k exec client -n web -- wget -qO- -T 3 backend-svc

memorise: k get endpoints backend-svc -n web   # IP:wrongport
k exec client -n web -- wget -qO- -T 3 backend-svc
k edit svc backend-svc -n web   # targetPort: 80
k exec client -n web -- wget -qO- -T 3 backend-svc

8.pattern: kubectl fails → crictl logs apiserver → fix static manifest

clues.means: API server is down: use crictl, not kubectl
Look in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml

traps: Trying kubectl/k logs while the API is down — use crictl ps -a / crictl logs
Restarting kubelet or moving the file — just save and wait up to 60 s
Changing etcd-servers to 2380 — etcd clients use 2379

verify.cmd: k get pods -n kube-system | grep apiserver

memorise: k get nodes   # retry every 15 s

9.pattern: New pods Pending, Node <none> → scheduler broken → fix manifest

clues.means: describe pod: no Events + Node <none> = nobody schedules it

clues.q: Other pods that were already running are fine
clues.means: Control plane partly OK; check kube-scheduler in kube-system

traps: Deleting/recreating test — the pod is fine, the scheduler is not
Editing the scheduler pod with kubectl edit — edit the static manifest file
Restarting kubelet instead of just saving and waiting

verify.cmd: k get pods -n kube-system | grep scheduler

10.pattern: Traffic times out → deny policy → add allow NetworkPolicy

clues.q: Do not delete or change any existing NetworkPolicy
clues.means: Add a new policy; policies are additive
from.podSelector must match only client (run=client)
ports: protocol TCP, port 80

traps: Using namespaceSelector instead of podSelector → lets every pod in
Selecting the client in spec.podSelector — spec.podSelector picks the backend pods (app=backend)
Leaving egress in policyTypes from the docs example

verify.cmd: k exec client -n web -- wget -qO- -T 3 backend-svc

memorise: k get pods -n web --show-labels   # backend app=backend, client run=client
docs: 'network policies' → copy example → keep ingress only
name: allow-client; podSelector app=backend; from podSelector run=client; ports TCP 80
k exec client -n web -- wget -qO- -T 3 backend-svc

11.pattern: Names don't resolve, IPs work → CoreDNS down → scale it

clues.means: DNS problem: check CoreDNS pods in kube-system (label k8s-app=kube-dns)

clues.q: Connections by IP address still work
clues.means: Network/CNI is fine; only DNS is broken

clues.q: Two CoreDNS replicas must be running
clues.means: Scale deploy coredns to exactly 2

traps: Looking for pods named dns in default namespace — CoreDNS lives in kube-system
Restarting pods when the deployment is scaled to 0
Forgetting --rm on the test pod, leaving pod t behind

12.pattern: Write command output to a file (logs, top)

clues.means: Redirect with > into exactly that path

clues.q: uses the most CPU across all namespaces
clues.means: k top pods -A --sort-by=cpu, take the first row
Only the pod name, nothing else

traps: Forgetting -A, so only default namespace is compared
Writing the whole top table into /opt/top.txt instead of just the name
Missing -n app on k logs → pod not found

13.pattern: ServiceAccount + Role + RoleBinding, imperative, then auth can-i

clues.means: Every command gets -n dev
--verb=get,list,create --resource=deployments

clues.q: binds the Role to the ServiceAccount
clues.means: --serviceaccount=dev:deploy-bot (NAMESPACE:NAME)

traps: Writing --serviceaccount=deploy-bot without dev: — no error, but it doesn't work
Spaces in --verb list
Forgetting -n dev on the role or binding

verify.cmd: k auth can-i create deployments -n dev --as=system:serviceaccount:dev:deploy-bot
k auth can-i delete deployments -n dev --as=system:serviceaccount:dev:deploy-bot

memorise: k auth can-i create deployments -n dev --as=system:serviceaccount:dev:deploy-bot

clues.means: Only the SA is namespaced: k create sa -n ops; serviceaccount=ops:node-viewer
--verb=get,list --resource=nodes (nodes are cluster-scoped)
Not a RoleBinding — nodes need cluster scope

traps: Using a RoleBinding — nodes are not namespaced, so it won't grant access
Adding -n to the clusterrole commands and thinking it matters
Wrong --serviceaccount format (must be ops:node-viewer)

15.pattern: helm template with a --set value into a file

clues.means: helm repo add argocd <url>

clues.q: The CRDs must NOT be installed by the chart
clues.means: Find the values key: helm show values | grep crds → --set crds.install=false
helm template … > /root/argo-helm.yaml (template, not install)

traps: Running helm install instead of helm template
Using --skip-crds (only affects crds/ folder) instead of crds.install=false for this chart
Forgetting --version 7.7.3 or --namespace argocd
memorise: helm repo add argocd https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm; helm repo update
helm template argocd argocd/argo-cd --version 7.7.3 --namespace argocd --set crds.install=false > /root/argo-helm.yaml

16.pattern: helm install → upgrade → rollback a release

clues.means: -n demo --create-namespace
--set controller.replicaCount=2 (find the key with helm show values)

clues.q: Roll the release back to revision `1`
clues.means: helm rollback web 1 -n demo

traps: Setting replicaCount instead of controller.replicaCount
Forgetting -n demo on upgrade/history/rollback → release not found
Expecting REVISION 1 after rollback — it becomes revision 3
memorise: helm repo add ingress-nginx https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx; helm repo update
helm install web ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx -n demo --create-namespace --set controller.replicaCount=2
helm upgrade web ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx -n demo --set controller.replicaCount=3
helm rollback web 1 -n demo; helm history web -n demo

17.pattern: Change Kustomize overlay, not base; apply with -k

clues.means: Change replicas count in kustomization.yaml to 3
k apply -k /root/kust (not -f)
Only touch kustomization.yaml

traps: Using k apply -f deploy.yaml (skips the namespace and replica patch)
Editing deploy.yaml
Checking the default namespace — kustomization sets namespace kust

18.pattern: List CRDs / explain a custom field into files

clues.means: k get crd | grep cert-manager > /root/crds.txt
k explain certificate.spec.subject > /root/subject.txt

traps: Using k get certificates (instances) instead of k get crd
Explaining certificate.subject (missing spec)
Typing the output instead of redirecting with >

19.pattern: Prepare node: install .deb, enable service, persistent sysctl

clues.means: dpkg -i /root/cri-dockerd.deb
systemctl enable --now cri-docker

clues.q: so that they persist across reboots
clues.means: Write a file in /etc/sysctl.d/, then sysctl --system (not sysctl -w)

traps: Using sysctl -w — lost after reboot
Service name is cri-docker, not cri-dockerd
Retyping parameters with typos instead of copying them

verify.cmd: systemctl is-active cri-docker; systemctl is-enabled cri-docker

20.pattern: Install CNI from manifest; NetworkPolicy needed → Calico

clues.means: Pick by the requirement, install only one
Flannel can't enforce NetworkPolicy → choose Calico

traps: Installing Flannel — it does not enforce NetworkPolicy
k apply on the tigera-operator file → 'annotations: Too long'; use k create
Leaving the default 192.168.0.0/16 cidr instead of the cluster's --cluster-cidr
memorise: k -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-controller-manager -o yaml | grep cluster-cidr
k apply -f custom-resources.yaml; k get nodes

21.pattern: kubeadm upgrade: drain → kubeadm → kubelet → uncordon, per node

clues.q: Upgrade the control plane node to Kubernetes `1.35.2`
clues.means: Control plane first: kubeadm upgrade apply v1.35.2
On node01: kubeadm upgrade node (not apply)

clues.q: Drain each node before upgrading it and make it schedulable again afterwards
clues.means: k drain … --ignore-daemonsets before, k uncordon after

traps: Running kubeadm upgrade apply on the worker — workers use kubeadm upgrade node
Forgetting apt-mark unhold/hold, so apt refuses to install
Forgetting daemon-reload + restart kubelet, so VERSION stays old
Running k drain/uncordon from node01 (no kubeconfig there) — run them on the control plane

verify.see: VERSION v1.35.2 on controlplane and node01

memorise: apt-mark unhold kubeadm; apt-get install -y kubeadm='1.35.2-*'; apt-mark hold kubeadm
kubeadm upgrade apply v1.35.2   # worker: kubeadm upgrade node
apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl; apt-get install -y kubelet='1.35.2-*' kubectl='1.35.2-*'; apt-mark hold kubelet kubectl

22.pattern: etcd snapshot save (with certs) + restore + repoint hostPath

clues.means: --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 plus cacert/cert/key from etcd.yaml
etcdctl snapshot save /opt/etcd-backup.db
In etcd.yaml change the etcd-data hostPath to /var/lib/etcd-restored

traps: Using the peer-cert/peer-key files instead of server.crt/server.key
Changing --data-dir or the mountPath instead of only the hostPath path
Panicking when kubectl is silent for ~60 s after saving etcd.yaml

verify.cmd: k get pods -n kube-system | grep etcd

23.pattern: Add containerPort, expose as NodePort with fixed nodePort

clues.means: k edit deploy: add ports: - containerPort: 80 protocol: TCP under the container
k expose … --type=NodePort
k expose can't set it: k edit svc → nodePort: 30080

traps: Wrong indentation of ports: (must line up with image:)
Leaving the random nodePort from k expose
Forgetting -n web

verify.cmd: k get deploy np -n web -o jsonpath='{..ports}'

memorise: k edit deploy np -n web   # under image: ports: - containerPort: 80 / protocol: TCP
k edit svc np-svc -n web   # nodePort: 30080

clues.means: k get ingressclass → --class=<name>
In --rule use /* (star = Prefix)

clues.q: must go to service `backend-svc` on port `80`
clues.means: =backend-svc:80

traps: Writing host/ instead of host/* → creates pathType Exact
Forgetting --class, so no controller picks it up
Forgetting quotes around --rule

25.pattern: Ingress → Gateway + HTTPRoute (copy host, TLS, rules)

clues.means: k get gatewayclass → gatewayClassName

clues.q: keeps the same hostname and TLS configuration as the Ingress
clues.means: Listener: protocol HTTPS, port 443, hostname, tls.certificateRefs = Ingress secretName

clues.q: keeps the same routing rules as the Ingress
clues.means: HTTPRoute: parentRefs web-gw, hostnames, path, backendRefs service:port
k delete ing web-ing -n web — only after route is created

traps: Forgetting the tls block (mode: Terminate + certificateRefs) on the listener
parentRefs name not matching web-gw
Forgetting namespace: web in both YAMLs

verify.cmd: k describe httproute web-route -n web | grep -A3 'Parent Refs'

memorise: k get ing web-ing -n web -o yaml   # host, secretName, path, service, port
docs: 'gateway api' → copy Gateway example → listener HTTPS 443 + hostname + tls: mode Terminate, certificateRefs: - name <secret>
docs: copy HTTPRoute example → parentRefs web-gw, hostnames, path, backendRefs
k apply -f gw.yaml -f route.yaml; k delete ing web-ing -n web

26.pattern: NetworkPolicy: allow pod label A → pod label B on one port

clues.means: spec.podSelector.matchLabels app: db

clues.q: ONLY from pods with label `app=api` in the same namespace
clues.means: from: - podSelector app: api (no namespaceSelector)
ports: - protocol: TCP port: 80

traps: Leaving namespaceSelector/ipBlock from the docs example in the from list
Putting podSelector and namespaceSelector as two list items (OR) instead of removing it
Keeping Egress in policyTypes → blocks db's outgoing traffic

verify.cmd: k exec api -n prod -- wget -qO- -T 3 db-svc | head -3
k exec other -n prod -- wget -qO- -T 3 db-svc

memorise: docs: 'network policies' → copy example → delete Egress, ipBlock, namespaceSelector, egress
name: db-policy; namespace: prod; podSelector app: db; from podSelector app: api; ports TCP 80

27.pattern: Default deny both directions + egress exception for DNS

clues.q: blocks all incoming and all outgoing traffic
clues.means: podSelector: {} and policyTypes Ingress + Egress

clues.q: for every pod in the namespace
clues.means: podSelector: {} (empty = all)
egress: - ports: UDP 53 and TCP 53 (no 'to', so any destination)

traps: Adding an empty ingress rule '- {}' which ALLOWS all ingress
Only UDP 53 — TCP 53 is also required
Forgetting namespace: prod in metadata

verify.see: Ingress: none allowed; Egress: to port 53/UDP, 53/TCP

verify.cmd: k exec app -n prod -- nslookup kubernetes.default
k exec app -n prod -- wget -qO- -T 3 kubernetes.default:443

memorise: docs: 'network policies' → 'Default deny all ingress and all egress traffic' example
name: default-deny; namespace: prod; podSelector: {}; policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
egress: - ports: - protocol: UDP port: 53 / - protocol: TCP port: 53
k apply -f deny.yaml; k describe netpol default-deny -n prod

28.pattern: Edit ConfigMap → rollout restart so pods pick it up

clues.means: ssl_protocols TLSv1.3; (remove TLSv1.2)

clues.q: make sure the running pods use the new configuration
clues.means: k rollout restart deploy nginx-static — pods don't reload the CM by themselves

traps: Not restarting the deployment — old config stays in nginx
Deleting the trailing ; → nginx fails to start
Editing the deployment instead of the ConfigMap

verify.cmd: k get cm nginx-config -n nginx-static -o yaml | grep ssl_protocols
k rollout status deploy nginx-static -n nginx-static

memorise: k get cm nginx-config -n nginx-static -o yaml > /root/cm-backup.yaml
k edit cm nginx-config -n nginx-static   # ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;
k rollout restart deploy nginx-static -n nginx-static
k rollout status deploy nginx-static -n nginx-static

clues.q: resolves to the service `backend-svc` in namespace `web`
clues.means: Target name backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local

clues.q: for all pods in the cluster
clues.means: Edit the coredns ConfigMap in kube-system (not a pod's /etc/hosts)

clues.q: Make sure CoreDNS uses the new configuration
clues.means: k rollout restart deploy coredns -n kube-system

traps: Putting the rewrite line outside the .:53 { } block or with broken indentation → CoreDNS CrashLoop
Rewriting to backend-svc without .web.svc.cluster.local
Not backing up the ConfigMap first
memorise: k get cm coredns -n kube-system -o yaml > /root/coredns-backup.yaml
k edit cm coredns -n kube-system   # under ready: rewrite name api.example.com backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local
k rollout restart deploy coredns -n kube-system
